title: 'Isha, the night prayer
tomorrow: the morning had its own words. does the evening get some too?

cards: Midnight. The room is dark except for a phone, and the phone is open to a forum where strangers guess when college decisions will drop. 'Isha was prayed hours ago. Nothing new has been posted in twenty minutes.
Refresh. The night prayer has an answer for this hour, and it's shorter than the forum thread: pray, then stop.

teach.h: ONCE THE LAST LIGHT IS GONE.
teach.b: 'Isha is the night prayer, once the last light has left the sky.

teach.h: NO SLEEP BEFORE, NO TALK AFTER.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, a companion reports that the Prophet ﷺ disliked sleeping before 'Isha and talking after it. Not forbidden. Disliked.
The prayer closes the day, and the day is supposed to stay closed.
In Sahih Muslim there's a gift attached: whoever prays 'Isha in congregation, it's as if they stood in prayer half the night. Night, then rest. That's the whole frame now, one post at a time.
Fifty became five, and the day got a frame. Fajr, said to someone still in bed: prayer is better than sleep. The morning adhkar, before sunrise or anywhere in the morning: morning, remembered.
Dhuhr, cool water in the rush: the midday pause. 'Asr, the one the afternoon tries to swallow: guard the middle prayer. Maghrib, a door at sunset that more than one family stands at.
And 'Isha, the last post, and then the lamp goes out. Five prayers, and one long breath between each.

how: 'Isha is prayed after the twilight has gone, and its time runs late into the night; Muslims often pray it at the mosque or at home before going to bed, and some add the short witr prayer after it.

o: a voluntary prayer said only in the last third of night
the dawn prayer, said in the dark before sunrise
the night prayer, said once the last light is gone

games.q: the week's frame — tap the pairs.

s: the Prophet disliked sleeping before 'Isha and talking after it
a report in Sahih al-Bukhari. disliked, not forbidden: the prayer closes the day.
once 'Isha is prayed, the rest of the night is for whatever you like
the prayer closes the day, and the day is supposed to stay closed. night, then rest.

games.q: an early shift tomorrow. 'Isha has come in and you're already yawning. what order fits the night?
o: sleep now, and set an alarm for midnight to pray 'Isha.
pray 'Isha now, wind down, and get to bed early.
stay up and pray it just before dawn to save a trip.
games.why: the Prophet disliked sleeping before 'Isha and talking after it. pray, then rest: the night prayer is the door that closes the day.

practice: Put the phone face down, or turn the screen off, and close your eyes. Let the day's noise run past once, like a train you're not getting on. When it's gone by, stay in the quiet that's left.

wordCard.voice: 'Isha: the night prayer, said once the last light leaves the sky, and the last word of this week's frame.

orig.note: Arabic: the night, the early dark; the last of the five daily prayers.

carryVoice: Last line of the week: night, then rest, the forum and all. Seven days, five posts, one frame.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 568 (the Prophet disliked sleeping before 'Isha and talking after it)
Sahih Muslim 656 (whoever prays 'Isha in congregation, it is as if he prayed half the night)
